messages:
Rae M.: FYI new dev laptop onboarding: curl installer fails when /usr/local/bin is a symlink to a mounted volume. Error: 'cannot create regular file '/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl' Permission denied' even when running with sudo. Any sane fallback flags?

Oli P.: That sounds like mount permissions. Workaround: install into ~/.local/bin or use `--dest` if the script supports it. Quick command I use: `mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && curl -L ... | tar -xO > ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl` then ensure PATH includes ~/.local/bin.

Tanya R.: We should add installer detection for non-writable dests and suggest alternate dirs. Also, the config/profile merging bug popped up again: after migrating dotfiles people end up with duplicate [profile] name = "staging" tables. `redwoodctl login --profile staging` writes token into the first match, not the intended endpoint.

Rae M.: Confirmed. CI flaked because the job reused a shared home. Workaround: set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=/tmp/redwood-config-$CI_JOB_ID` in CI. Filed quick note in the onboarding doc.

infra-bot: Tip: for non-interactive auth, prefer `redwoodctl login --token-file /secrets/redwood_token` or `--token-stdin`. Ensure the file is readable by the job user.

Oli P.: Also ran into headless SSO with `redwoodctl dev --local` blocking on browser open. We need `--no-browser` and `--token-stdin` well-documented. Can we standardize both flags?

Tanya R.: Agreed. Proposal: expose `--no-browser`, `--token-file`, `--token-stdin`, and env knobs `REDWOODCTL_AUTH_RETRIES` and `REDWOODCTL_MAX_CONCURRENT_AUTH` to help CI avoid IdP 429s. I'll open an issue with minimal repro and suggested flags.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2775 "installer: fallback dests; config duplicate profiles causing login ambiguity; headless auth flags & CI knobs" by Tanya R. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2775

Rae M.: Thanks — adding the ~/.local/bin install snippet and the REDWOODCTL_CONFIG CI pattern to the new-hire doc now. :thumbsup:
